facts.text: On this date in 1889, Nellie Bly left New York to circle the globe in under 80 days — she did it in 72, beating Phileas Fogg's fictional record and filing dispatches the whole way.

On this date in 1969, Apollo 12 launched — the second Moon landing is so overshadowed by Apollo 11 that most people cannot name a single astronaut from it. It was Pete Conrad, Alan Bean, and Richard Gordon.
Manila is the world's most densely populated city proper, packing over 70,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any place on Earth, including Hong Kong or Dhaka.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka with a 4,000 km radius than live outside it — roughly half of all humanity fits within that one boundary.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding about 60% of the world's fresh surface lake water within its borders.
On this day in 1972, the Dow Jones closed above 1,000 for the first time. It had taken the index 76 years to reach that milestone. It would cross 2,000 just 15 years later.

On this day in 1910, the first aircraft landing on a US Navy ship was tested — triggering a century of defense contracts that now make Lockheed Martin's annual revenue larger than the GDP of 130 countries.
The NYSE's smallest ever recorded trade: one share of Berkshire Hathaway Class A, which as of 2024 costs more than a median American home. The stock has never split.

When the Weimar Republic's hyperinflation peaked in 1923, a wheelbarrow full of banknotes couldn't buy a newspaper. The currency lost so much value that some factories paid workers twice a day so they could shop at lunch before prices rose.

Saudi Aramco briefly held a $2 trillion market cap in 2019 — making it worth more than Apple, Google, and Microsoft combined at that moment. It got there after the world's largest IPO raised $25.6 billion.
On this date in 1969, Apollo 12 launched — and was struck by lightning twice within 36 seconds of liftoff. The crew kept flying.
Your bones are constantly dissolving and rebuilding. Every decade, you have an almost entirely new skeleton.
On this date in 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit another planet. It arrived at Mars to find a global dust storm — and simply waited.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
The mantis shrimp sees 16 types of color receptors to your three — yet processes color worse than you do. Evolution built the hardware, then skipped the software.
On this day in 1889, Nellie Bly left New York to circle the globe in 72 days — beating Phileas Fogg's fictional record from a novel published just 16 years earlier.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded.
On this day in 1969, Apollo 12 launched — the second Moon landing, now closer in time to the Wright Brothers' first flight than to today.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landings than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
The fax machine was invented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, 140 years before most offices ever used one.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a place you cannot return to — or that never existed. English has no equivalent, which is itself a kind of hiraeth.
Sonder (coined 2012): the realization that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. It spread so fast linguists debate whether it qualifies as a real word yet.
On this day in 1851, Melville published Moby-Dick to indifferent reviews. The word 'ungodly' appears 11 times. 'Whiteness' appears more than any color in a novel obsessed with black and white.
Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): a look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The language has fewer than five fluent speakers left.
On this day in 1940, Coventry was bombed so completely that Germans coined a verb: 'coventrisieren' — to raze a city by air. The word outlived the regime that made it.

On this date in 2017, Bitcoin hit $7,000 for the first time — but more quietly, SegWit adoption crossed 10% of transactions that same week, a protocol shift that had taken years of civil war to force through.

On Nov 14, 2022, FTX's on-chain wallets drained $477M in suspicious outflows hours after bankruptcy filing. Blockchain's transparency exposed the theft in real time — something no traditional bank collapse ever offered.
Ethereum's gas limit is not a fixed protocol rule. Validators vote on it block-by-block, and they've raised it 9x since launch without a hard fork.

Bitcoin's timelock opcode, CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, sat in the codebase as a disabled no-op for years before BIP 65 activated it in 2015 — meaning locked funds were always possible, just deliberately switched off.

The Ethereum genesis block contains a hidden message in its extra data field: a reference to a 2015 Guardian headline about bank bailouts, mirroring Satoshi's own embedded headline in Bitcoin's block zero.
On this date in 2016, DeepMind's AlphaGo defeated European champion Fan Hui 5-0 — the first time a computer beat a professional Go player without handicap, years ahead of expert predictions.
On this date in 1985, the first Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) conference was proposed; it now receives over 15,000 paper submissions annually.
GPT-4 was trained on roughly 25,000 A100 GPUs for an estimated 90 days. The electricity alone cost more than most nations spend annually on scientific research.
RLHF — the technique that made ChatGPT feel coherent — was originally developed to align simulated robots in 2017. Its application to language models was considered a long shot by its own authors.
The transformer architecture, now the backbone of nearly every frontier AI system, was introduced in a 2017 paper by eight authors. Six of them have since left Google.
